clients.name: Hallow Tix
clients.stack: Next.js, Node.js API, Postgres, Redis, Stripe checkout
clients.persona: nervous, still traumatized by last year's 6pm crash
constraints: Every ticket is a numbered entry for one timed slot: it can be sold exactly once
The release starts exactly at 6pm and is announced on social media, so traffic arrives all at once
Checkout goes through Stripe; a charge without a ticket means a refund and an angry customer

memories.solution: Scaled the web servers way up right before the release
memories.what_broke: The site crashed within 90 seconds. Every new server opened its own database connections and Postgres hit its connection limit, so every page failed
memories.fix: Restarted with fewer servers and ran the sale again the next day
memories.outcome: Lost a night of sales and a lot of trust. Lesson: more servers did not help; the database was the bottleneck

memories.request: Send reminder emails before a release
memories.solution: Scheduled emails 24 hours and 1 hour before the release, sent in batches
memories.what_broke: The first batch hit the email provider's rate limit

memories.solution: Enabled it through Stripe's payment element
memories.what_broke: Nothing. It worked on the first try

clients.name: Costume Cauldron
clients.stack: Next.js storefront, serverless functions, DynamoDB, CDN
clients.persona: cocky and breezy, loves saying 'just autoscale'
constraints: Costumes have stock counts in the thousands, not unique seats
Product pages must load in under a second

memories.request: Survive a Halloween flash sale with 20,000 shoppers at once
memories.solution: Cached every product page at the CDN and let the serverless functions autoscale on their own
memories.what_broke: Nothing. The CDN served most pages and serverless scaled by itself; the site never went down
memories.outcome: Biggest sales day ever. Note: our items are plentiful stock, not one-of-a-kind seats

memories.solution: Built a five-question quiz that recommends a size
memories.what_broke: Returns did not drop until we added real measurements
memories.fix: Asked for height and chest size

memories.solution: Sent one reminder email two hours after a cart was left
memories.what_broke: Reminders went out for items already sold out

clients.name: Pumpkin Patch Pass
clients.persona: anxious and cautionary, haunted by the double-booking disaster
constraints: Each timed-entry slot has a fixed capacity
Families must get a confirmation within a minute of paying

memories.request: Sell timed-entry tickets for opening weekend without double booking
memories.solution: Checked if a slot was free, then charged the card, then saved the booking
memories.what_broke: Tickets were sold twice. Two buyers passed the availability check at the same moment and both got the last spots, so 300 families showed up for 150 places
memories.fix: Reserve the ticket in the database first, as a hold that expires after 10 minutes, then charge; a unique rule per ticket makes selling the same ticket twice impossible
memories.outcome: No double bookings since. We refunded and apologized to 150 families

memories.request: Text families their entry QR code
memories.solution: Sent the code by SMS right after payment
memories.what_broke: Some carriers flagged the messages as spam

memories.solution: Allowed one free change up to 24 hours before

clients.name: Candy Courier
clients.persona: battle-scarred veteran, blunt, 'been there, it broke'
constraints: Delivery slots are limited per neighborhood
Drivers' app must keep working during peak

memories.request: Survive the Halloween-night rush of 50,000 people booking delivery slots at once
memories.solution: Let Kubernetes autoscale the API servers as traffic grew
memories.what_broke: Autoscaling made it worse. The new servers all hit the same database, it locked up and crashed, and then every server retried at once and knocked it over again
memories.fix: Put a virtual waiting room in front: let people in only as fast as the database can handle and show each person their place in line; added rate limits and backoff on retries
memories.outcome: The next year's rush stayed up at three times the traffic

memories.request: Track drivers live on a map
memories.solution: Drivers' phones sent their location every 10 seconds
memories.fix: Sent location only while a delivery was active

memories.request: Notify customers when candy is five minutes away
memories.solution: Push notification based on the driver's position
memories.what_broke: Notifications fired too early in dense neighborhoods
memories.fix: Used road distance instead of straight-line distance
memories.outcome: Arrival estimates are now accurate to a minute

clients.name: Ghost Tour Co.
clients.stack: React Native app, Firebase, offline audio
clients.persona: spooky and theatrical, speaks in short eerie lines
constraints: Tours run in cellars and graveyards with no signal

memories.request: Play audio stories offline in cellars with no signal
memories.solution: Downloaded each tour's audio when the guest opened the app
memories.what_broke: Downloads failed on slow hotel wifi
memories.fix: Downloaded in small pieces and resumed after drops

memories.request: Trigger a story when guests reach a graveyard spot
memories.solution: Used GPS zones around each stop
memories.what_broke: GPS drifted near tall old buildings
memories.fix: Added a tap-to-start button as a backup

memories.request: Offer tour scripts in four languages
memories.solution: Stored every script per language in the app
memories.what_broke: Nothing. Guests picked their language at start
memories.outcome: Half of guests now choose a non-English tour
